Wild tensors and tensor pattern matching

Source: R/tensor-wild.R
wild-tensors.Rd

Ports of SymPy's WildTensorIndex, WildTensorHead and WildTensor. A WildTensorIndex matches any index of its index type, of the same variance unless ignore_updown = TRUE. A WildTensorHead is called like a tensor head; the result, a WildTensor, matches any tensor expression whose free indices match its indices (in any order when unordered_indices = TRUE), and with no indices it matches any tensor expression. sym_match() matches a tensor expression against a pattern and sym_replace() replaces the matches, as expr.match() and expr.replace() do in SymPy; a matched wild tensor head stands for the matched expression with its free indices renamed (SymPy's _WildTensExpr).

Usage

WildTensorIndex(name, tensor_index_type, is_up = TRUE, ignore_updown = FALSE)

WildTensorHead(
  name,
  index_types = NULL,
  symmetry = NULL,
  comm = 0,
  unordered_indices = FALSE
)

Arguments

name

The name of the index or head.

tensor_index_type

A TensorIndexType.

is_up

Whether the index is contravariant.

ignore_updown

Whether the index matches indices of either variance.

index_types, symmetry, comm

As for TensorHead(); the index types of a wild tensor are those of its indices, and wild heads have no symmetry.

unordered_indices

Whether the indices of the wild tensor match in any order.

Value

A wild index or a wild tensor head.

Examples

R3 <- TensorIndexType("R3", dim = 3)
idx <- tensor_indices("p q", R3)
p <- idx$p; q <- idx$q
a <- WildTensorIndex("a", R3, ignore_updown = TRUE)
K <- TensorHead("K", list(R3)); V <- TensorHead("V", list(R3))
W <- WildTensorHead("W", unordered_indices = TRUE)
sym_match(K(p) * V(q), W(a, p))
#> $a
#> q 
#> 
#> $`W(R3,R3)`
#> _WildTensExpr(K(p)*V(q)) 
#> 
sym_replace(K(p) * V(-p), W(a) * V(-a), 1)
#> 1
sym_replace(K(p) * V(q), W(q) * K(p), W(p) * W(q))
#> V(p)*V(q)
